clue.text: Off Aden, tar moves from bow to stern?

indicators.note: the letters of the sailor's phrase move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor somewhere off the port of Aden walks the length of the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' looks like the sailor doing the moving, but with 'Off Aden' it is just anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical phrase meaning lengthwise along a vessel, spanning its whole length from front to back.

parts.note: Americans call autumn by this word, which also means a drop or decline

explanation.surface: An economic dip that hits American business every year at the same season.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue pretends to be about trade figures; it is the American word for autumn, which is also a slump.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans name autumn after leaves dropping, and a slump is a drop, so one word covers both.

clue.text: Soldiers should meet general coming back

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
general in the sense of widespread or prevailing, as a current belief is

explanation.surface: Troops are due to rendezvous with their returning commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer, but it is the adjective meaning prevailing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that keeps happening again repeats over and over, returning at intervals.

clue.text: In the lead — by so much?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a winning margin of one horse's head in a race

explanation.definitionFit: Being in front is an everyday sense; split in two it names a racing margin of a single head.

parts.note: an urging 'do!', as in 'do come'
a wager is a bet, so 'do wager' urges someone to place one

explanation.surface: A widow urges someone to have a flutter.
explanation.definitionFit: A titled widow holding property or rank from her late husband is a dowager.

parts.note: to fan is to cool with a stream of air
to club is to beat with a stick

explanation.surface: A band's backing singers lay down a cool rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing group' suggests musicians behind a singer, but it means supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: An organised body of admirers supports a star, so it backs them.

clue.text: Grand old politician with the gift of the gab

definitions.text: with the gift of the gab

parts.note: a Lib is a Liberal, the British party that preceded the Liberal Democrats

explanation.surface: An elderly statesman who was always a smooth talker.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluent but shallow speech is the mark of someone too ready with words, a smooth talker.

parts.note: a pride is the collective noun for a group of these big cats

explanation.surface: People strut about full of self-satisfaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride' seems to be vanity; it is a family group of big cats.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cats of the savannah live and travel in groups called prides.

definitions.meaning: to detain someone in conversation against their will
a flower worn in the lapel slot, a rose being one example

explanation.definitionFit: One word is both a verb for accosting someone and a flower pinned to a jacket lapel.

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

indicators.note: lounged wobbles its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman sprawls unsteadily in his gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a place to lounge, but it is the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy cudgel used as a weapon is a club, a synonym.

clue.text: Money is bait that takes many in

indicators.note: with 'in', the bait word takes something into itself
completes 'takes in', the bait word holding the numeral

parts.note: a lure is a bait used to attract
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

explanation.surface: Cash is the lure that draws in the crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: Filthy lucre is an old, disparaging word for money, a synonym.

parts.note: a winkle is a small edible sea snail
out is the opposite of in

explanation.surface: A seafood fan asks whether the shellfish isn't inside its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: To prise something out with effort, like a pin drawing a snail from its shell, means to extract.

clue.text: Egg on single girl to be spendthrift

parts.note: to prod is to urge or egg on
I is the Roman numeral one
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: Someone urges an unmarried woman to splash out.
explanation.definitionFit: Wastefully extravagant, like the son in the parable who squandered his inheritance.

parts.note: Di is short for Diana, so Diana's gives Di's
Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Diana's company puts on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A night of dancing to recorded pop music is a form of entertainment.

clue.text: England supporter offers misplaced help in goal

indicators.note: the letters of three words are put in the wrong places

explanation.surface: A football fan offers some badly placed assistance in the goalmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'England supporter' looks like a football fan, but it is a lover of things English.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who admires English culture and customs supports England in a broad sense.

clue.text: To want that is right, though comparatively broke?

parts.note: to want is to need
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Is it fair to be in need when you're poorer than others?
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative adjective: poorer, more in want than someone else, so broke to a greater degree.

indicators.note: the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Eric dropped by for pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen sweet made with cream is a common pudding course.

indicators.note: with the question mark, 'of' means made out of these letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: A tribute to Shakespeare's range.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the Bard is fodder: his title's letters make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Range or extent, the width of something, is its scope.

clue.text: Feeble joke in cracker not dry enough to work?

definitions.text: Feeble joke in cracker not dry enough to work?

parts.words: Feeble joke in cracker not dry enough to work?
parts.note: a squib is a small firework, and a wet one fizzles out, so a disappointment

explanation.surface: The weak joke inside a Christmas cracker that falls flat.
explanation.walkthrough: A Christmas cracker is a paper tube pulled at British Christmas dinners, holding a bad joke; here 'cracker' is a firework.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet firework fails to go off, so the idiom means an anticlimax or flop.

definitions.meaning: people who rent out property, one who lets

explanation.definitionFit: Read as 'those who let', landlords; as alphabet symbols, characters of writing.

indicators.note: revised means altered, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Only one portion was ever changed.
explanation.definitionFit: A division or segment of a whole is a part of it.

parts.note: the Mini is a small British car
mal is French for illness, as in mal de mer

explanation.surface: Travel sickness on a car journey is hardly noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest possible amount, barely anything, means very little.

clue.text: Rotational forces — they last only a short time

definitions.meaning: in physics, turning effects of a force about a pivot

definitions.text: they last only a short time

explanation.definitionFit: The physics term for turning effects of force is also the plural of a brief instant.
One word covers both authority over people and physical strength or energy.

clue.text: Thin disc made of iron used in fighting

indicators.note: the symbol is placed within the fighting word

parts.note: war is armed fighting
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A slim shield forged of iron for battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A communion host or a silicon slice is a very thin round piece, a flat disc.

clue.text: It's soothing when you have to concentrate

definitions.meaning: a pad of cloth pressed on an injury to relieve it
to squeeze into a smaller space

explanation.definitionFit: A noun for a soothing pad pressed on a wound and a verb for squeezing tightly together.

definitions.meaning: the scope of a body's brief or responsibility

explanation.definitionFit: A verb for deferring a penalty and a noun for the scope of an assigned task.

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the two words that follow, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A driver took a different route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drove' seems to be a verb; it is a noun for a group of cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a group of animals moved along together, a synonym for a flock of cattle.

clue.text: Dilapidated inn to fail in time of price increases

indicators.note: dilapidated means falling apart, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A run-down pub is bound to go under when costs keep rising.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of generally rising prices and falling purchasing power, in economic terms.

clue.text: Computer device doctor has to operate

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
to use a machine is to operate it

explanation.surface: A surgeon must use a gadget to perform surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operate' suggests surgery after 'doctor', but it means work a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The handheld pointing gadget used with a PC is one example of a computer device.

parts.note: the organs of hearing take in noise, not things that are reliable

explanation.surface: Sensible people agree to whatever is reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' seems to mean sensible; it means noise, received by the organs of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The organs of hearing receive noise, taking in what is audible.

clue.text: Don boasted about revealing diarist's last words?

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A university lecturer bragged about what a famous diary disclosed.
explanation.walkthrough: The diarist is Samuel Pepys, who often ended a day's diary entry with this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepys closed many entries with this sign-off, so it was a diarist's final words of the day.
